ROLL — Movement Technique (Common)

A controlled tumble that redirects the force of an impact across the whole body instead of absorbing it through the legs alone.

Timed into a fall, a Roll bleeds off a portion of the impact before it ever reaches bone — the difference between a bruise and a broken leg.

The same motion, used on level ground, still carries you a short distance — useful, but it is the fall-timing this technique was built around.

A Roll started too early or too late does nothing. The body must already be falling for the technique to have anything to redirect.
